items.title: Pay the demanded 'Grunderfassung' / processing fee
items.quote: Zahlen Sie die Gebühr bis zum 29.07.2026 auf das Konto IBAN LT21 7044 0000 0447 1229
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment ('bis zum 29.07.2026'), so no period calculation is needed; the due date is simply the date as stated. (By the time this letter is being reviewed, today is 2026-10-01, so this date has in any case already passed.)

warnings: This letter shows the classic pattern of a 'Datenschutzregister' / GDPR-registration scam: Art. 30 DSGVO only obliges companies to keep their own internal record of processing activities ('Verzeichnis von Verarbeitungstätigkeiten') — there is no central German or EU authority that registers this, and no fee is ever owed for it.

The payment is to be sent to a Lithuanian IBAN (LT21 7044 0000 0447 1229) for a recipient named 'Registerservice M. Kovalenko', which does not match the sending company's name ('DSR Datenschutz-Registerstelle Europa UAB') — a strong sign the money would not go to a legitimate office.

The letter uses pressure tactics typical of scams: a very short payment deadline, a threat to report the recipient to a data-protection authority, and a threat of fines up to €20,000,000, which is far beyond what such a 'registration' could ever trigger.

The letter claims 'Ein Widerspruch gegen die Erfassung ist nicht möglich' (no objection is possible) — a genuine authority would give proper legal-remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung); flatly denying any right to object is itself a red flag.
The letter insists replies are accepted only by e-mail, discouraging phone or postal contact that could be used to verify its legitimacy through official channels.

Recommendation: do not pay, do not reply with personal or bank data, and verify independently (e.g. via the Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz or Verbraucherzentrale) before taking any action; this assessment is information, not legal advice.
